extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media organisations, media regulators, policymakers and members of the public interested in press standards and regulation in India
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts standards, evaluative criteria and procedural norms used by the Press Council of India and related government/policy actors to judge or guide journalism, media governance, and media-facing processes in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of news and opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: "News should not be mixed with views."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Vice‑President and cited journalism stalwarts emphasise a clear 'Lakshman Rekha' between news and opinion; news must not be coloured by the reporter's or editor's personal views. Journalists should present factual accounts distinct from commentary or editorialising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unbiased, objective and truthful reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Good journalism hinges on unbiased and truthful coverage of events and their credible transmission to the people."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters must not compromise on facts and should present information "without fear or favour." The Council and speakers call for objective reporting as a foundational standard for a functioning democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism; focus on substantive coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Caution against sensationalising news and giving undue attention to disruptors; media should highlight constructive speeches in Parliament and legislatures instead of disruptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and newsrooms should prioritise meaningful debate and constructive coverage over dramatic or disruptive incidents that skew public perception; avoid disproportionate coverage of disruptions merely because they are sensational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to dignity and safety of women in media content
rubrics_metrics.description: "Complete sensitivity towards the dignity and safety of women in their advertisements, news and programmes is expected."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content (news, ads, programmes) should respect women's dignity and safety, avoid sexist or demeaning portrayals, and cultivate respect and sensitivity through editorial decisions and organisational culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active fact‑checking and combating misinformation (with safeguards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact‑check units (e.g., PIB) should fight fake news and misinformation; governments and institutions have mechanisms to combat fake news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While fact‑checking and countering misinformation is highlighted as essential (PIB example), mandatory government take‑down powers based solely on an agency's marking of content as 'fake' risk censorship; stakeholder consultation and balancing free‑speech safeguards are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public service broadcasting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Public broadcasters (Doordarshan, All India Radio) are recognised for delivering public service via prompt coverage, ground reports and public‑health programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcast organisations should prioritise access to awareness messages, government guidelines and free consultations (where relevant), reflecting a public‑service mandate rather than purely commercial priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety, protection and security of journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls for steps to protect journalists facing threats, imprisonment, violence and killings; creation of a safe and free environment for media workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governments, institutions and the international community should implement legal, practical and institutional measures (e.g., UN Plan of Action on Safety of Journalists) to prevent impunity, investigate attacks and ensure journalists' safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for an enforceable independent media regulator (suggestion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliamentary committee recommended exploring an umbrella statutory media body with powers to enforce directives and take punitive action for grave violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee argued that self‑regulatory mechanisms lack enforceability; it recommended a feasibility study to consider a unified regulator that is independent, impartial and able to respond to current media‑landscape challenges. The Ministry was asked to examine restructuring options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Council Act mandate and Code of Conduct (Norms of Journalistic Conduct, 2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 13(2)(b) of the Press Council Act enjoins the Council to build a code of conduct to help and guide print media in maintaining and improving professional standards; Norms of Journalistic Conduct 2022 has been updated and released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code is an explicit normative instrument intended to guide print media practice and professional standards; the 2022 edition updates previous norms (released on National Press Day). Specific norms are referenced as the Council's tool for guidance and adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint adjudication and grievance redressal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints against media persons are filed with the Press Council and disposed of through adjudication, mediation by the Chairperson, summary disposal for lack of grounds, withdrawal, or as sub‑judice; grievance redressal includes internal and external routes (Director of Grievances available Wednesdays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council operates processes for receiving and resolving complaints, records filings and disposals (Annexures referenced), and provides public access points (e.g., set times to meet Director of Grievances). Staff grievances are handled by a designated Staff Grievance Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and anti‑corruption mechanisms for the Council
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Press Council acts as Chief Vigilance Officer; a vigilance set‑up conducts regular and surprise checks to prevent/combat corruption; Vigilance Awareness Week observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal governance standards include proactive vigilance, inspections, and awareness initiatives to uphold integrity in council operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to Information (RTI) compliance and openness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council received RTI applications (180 during the period) and disposed of all during the review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely processing and disposal of RTI requests is presented as a measure of transparency and public accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories and dimensions for National Awards for Excellence in Journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: National Awards (2020) were conferred in ten categories (including Raja Ram Mohan Roy National Award, Rural Journalism, Reporting from Conflict Area, Best Newspaper Art: Covering Illustrations/Cartoons/Caricatures, Photojournalism single picture, Photo feature, Sports Reporting, Developmental Reporting, Financial Reporting, Gender Issue Reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These award categories imply evaluative dimensions and subject areas in which journalistic excellence is assessed; the report names winners as exemplars for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit‑based internship selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Winter Internship Programme (2023) selected ten interns from across the country based on their qualifications and compliance with necessary conditions, while promoting PAN‑India opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasises merit, eligibility compliance, geographic representation and the Council's objective to facilitate knowledge and responsibility among journalism students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of official language use (Hindi) in Council work
rubrics_metrics.description: Council promoted Hindi via Official Language Implementation Committee meetings, workshops, Hindi Fortnight/Diwas, Hindi publications and incentives under 'Hindi Protsahan Yojana'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraging official work in Hindi, recognising staff contributions with prizes/certificates, and publishing records in Hindi are treated as institutional language‑policy standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW) for public site usability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council's website was redeveloped in accordance with GIGW guidelines and relaunched to be more user friendly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with GIGW indicates standards for accessibility, usability and government web best practices when presenting council information to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate jurisdiction and procedural standards under Press & Registration law
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Section 8C of the Press & Registration of Books Act, 1867 the Press Council exercises appellate jurisdiction over magisterial orders of non‑authentication of a Declaration under Section 6 or its subsequent cancellation under Section 8B; an Appellate Board (chair + member) hears appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural structures (board composition, sittings, appeals disposed) define a formal appeals mechanism for registration matters and ensure legal remedies within the press‑registration regime.
